name: Cervical Radiculopathy
summary: Cervical radiculopathy means a cervical nerve root is irritated or compressed, causing arm symptoms that follow that root's pattern. The most commonly affected roots are C6 and C7.

looksLike: Neck and arm pain, usually arm pain more troublesome than neck pain.
Pins and needles, numbness or weakness in a root-specific pattern.
Worse with neck extension and turning to the painful side; may ease with hand on head.
Atypical features that point elsewhere: both arms or legs involved, clumsy hands, gait change, bladder change, constant night pain unrelated to position.
redFlags: Bilateral limb symptoms, gait change, clumsy hands, Hoffmann or Babinski
Progressive or severe motor loss (for example grade 3 or below, or worsening day to day)
Bladder or bowel change with limb signs
Trauma with midline tenderness or neurological signs
Fever, weight loss, cancer history, immunosuppression, night pain
Sudden severe headache with dizziness, double vision, speech or swallowing difficulty
firstSteps: Initial approach: education and active exercise, for stable mild to moderate cases.
Justifying findings: root-pattern signs, no red flags, mild stable deficit.
Priority: education, then movement and strengthening.

assess: Observation: posture, arm position, muscle wasting.
Active cervical movement: range and symptom response, especially rotation, extension.
Neurological examination: dermatomes (light touch), myotomes (resisted key movements), reflexes (biceps, brachioradialis, triceps). Compare sides.
Upper motor neuron screen (when history raises concern): Hoffmann sign, gait, tandem walk, lower limb reflexes, clonus, Babinski.
Shoulder and elbow screen to exclude local mimics.

tests.name: Spurling test (compression)
tests.purpose: Check whether foraminal narrowing reproduces the patient's arm symptoms
tests.positive: Reproduction of the patient's usual arm symptoms. Neck-only pain is not counted as positive by most descriptions
procedure: Step 1: patient actively side-bends to the symptomatic side and extends slightly. Step 2: therapist places hands on top of the head and applies gentle axial compression. Stop at the first symptom.
tests.interpretation: Positive supports radiculopathy, mainly as part of a cluster If positive with arm symptoms, do not repeat. Go to the distraction test and neurodynamic test

tests.name: Cervical distraction test
tests.purpose: Check whether reducing foraminal compression relieves arm symptoms
tests.positive: Arm symptoms clearly decrease or disappear
tests.patientPosition: Supine, head supported, symptoms present if possible
tests.therapistPosition: At the head end, hands under occiput and chin or mastoid area
procedure: Slowly apply upward traction along the neck axis, about gentle to moderate force, hold briefly
tests.interpretation: Positive supports radiculopathy. It also hints that traction may help A positive result makes traction or manual distraction worth considering in treatment

tests.name: Upper limb neurodynamic test A (median nerve bias, ULNT1)
tests.purpose: Check whether stretching the median nerve pathway reproduces arm symptoms
tests.positive: Reproduction of the usual symptoms, and change when the neck position changes (structural differentiation)
tests.patientPosition: Supine, arm at the side of the bench
procedure: 1) Depress shoulder girdle. 2) Abduct shoulder to about 90°. 3) Supinate forearm and extend wrist and fingers. 4) Externally rotate shoulder. 5) Extend elbow gradually to the first symptom. 6) Add contralateral then ipsilateral neck side-bend to differentiate

tests.name: Shoulder abduction relief sign (Bakody)
tests.positive: Arm symptoms ease within about a minute
procedure: Patient places the hand of the painful arm on top of the head
tests.interpretation: Reduced root tension, consistent with radiculopathy

book.title: Cervical Radiculopathy
book.lead: Model chapter. All later condition chapters follow this layout.

blocks.text: **Cervical radiculopathy** means a cervical nerve root is irritated or compressed, causing arm symptoms that follow that root's pattern. The most commonly affected roots are C6 and C7 [Ref – to verify]. Typical causes are disc herniation in younger adults and foraminal narrowing from degeneration in older adults. A nerve root exits through the intervertebral foramen. If this space narrows, or the disc material or inflammation contacts the root, the root may become sensitive and, in some people, conduct signals poorly. This is the leading explanation, but the exact pain mechanism varies between patients and is still debated.

items: Neck and arm pain, usually arm pain more troublesome than neck pain.
Pins and needles, numbness or weakness in a root-specific pattern.
Worse with neck extension and turning to the painful side; may ease with hand on head.
Atypical features that point elsewhere: both arms or legs involved, clumsy hands, gait change, bladder change, constant night pain unrelated to position.

blocks.text: Patterns overlap between people. Use them as clues, not proof.

**Active cervical movement:** range and symptom response, especially rotation, extension.
**Neurological examination:** dermatomes (light touch), myotomes (resisted key movements), reflexes (biceps, brachioradialis, triceps). Compare sides.

blocks.text: How to combine them

A published clinical prediction cluster used a combination of positive neurodynamic test, positive Spurling, positive distraction and limited ipsilateral rotation. More positives in the cluster raise the likelihood of radiculopathy [Ref – to verify exact criteria and likelihood ratios before teaching this as a rule]. A negative cluster lowers the likelihood but does not remove the need to consider other causes.

sections.title: G. RED FLAGS AND URGENT CONDITIONS

rows: Bilateral limb symptoms, gait change, clumsy hands, Hoffmann or Babinski
Stop manual techniques and compression tests; refer
Progressive or severe motor loss (for example grade 3 or below, or worsening day to day)
Bladder or bowel change with limb signs
Trauma with midline tenderness or neurological signs
Immobilize; use validated imaging decision rules per local protocol
Fever, weight loss, cancer history, immunosuppression, night pain
Sudden severe headache with dizziness, double vision, speech or swallowing difficulty
Stop; do not manipulate; emergency services

blocks.text: Defer: cervical manipulation, strong traction, compression testing and end-range loading until the red flag is resolved.

sections.title: H. Working diagnosis and decision pathway

items: Any emergency red flag? **Yes:** emergency action. **No:** go on.
Any myelopathy signs? **Yes:** urgent spine review. **No:** go on.

Arm-dominant pain with root-pattern sensory, motor or reflex signs, plus at least some positive cluster tests? **Yes:** working diagnosis is cervical radiculopathy. **No:** reconsider the differentials in Section F.
Is the motor deficit mild and stable? **Yes:** begin conservative care. **No (progressive or severe):** refer urgently while supporting the patient.

blocks.text: Supports the diagnosis: arm-dominant pain, matching neurological signs, positive cluster. Argues against: no neck movement effect, no neurological signs, bilateral symptoms. Must not miss: myelopathy, cardiac cause, tumour, infection, vascular event.

rows: May reduce arm symptoms in the short term [Ref – to verify]
Supine, gentle sustained traction along neck axis, 10 to 15 seconds, repeat a few times
Symptoms spread, dizziness, increased arm pain
Reduces stiffness; may help neck and arm pain [Ref – to verify]
Prone or sitting, graded central or unilateral glides
Positive neurodynamic test, symptoms mild to moderate
Gentle slider movements, avoid provoking strong symptoms
Symptoms last longer than a short time after treatment

blocks.text: **Preferred starting choice** for a stable, mild case: education plus active exercise, adding manual distraction only if the distraction test relieved symptoms. Evidence for manual therapy in radiculopathy is limited and the effects are mostly short term [Ref – to verify]. Do not claim that manual therapy corrects a disc or realigns bones. Avoid high-velocity manipulation in radiculopathy unless an experienced clinician has screened thoroughly. The risk-benefit balance is debated.
**Is it working?** Look for reduced arm symptoms, better rotation, and the same-session improvement in a named measure. If there is no change after two to three sessions, change approach.

Rotation and side-bend within comfortable range
Band rows, wall presses, then overhead loading
Moderate effort, no lasting arm symptoms

blocks.text: **Symptom rule:** neck ache that settles within a short time is acceptable. Arm symptoms moving further down the arm, or new numbness or weakness, means stop and reassess. This dosage is an illustration only. Adjust to symptoms, goals and tolerance.

sections.title: N. Clinical case and reasoning questions

blocks.text: **Case:** A 42-year-old teacher has right neck pain, arm pain to the thumb side for three weeks, and tingling in the thumb and index finger. No trauma, no fever, normal gait, no bladder change. Right wrist extension is 4/5, right brachioradialis reflex is reduced, rotation to the right is limited. Spurling reproduces arm symptoms. Distraction relieves them. Bakody relief is negative.

**Working diagnosis:** right C6 radiculopathy. Reason: arm-dominant pain, thumb-index sensory change, matching wrist extension weakness and reflex reduction, and a positive Spurling and distraction cluster. This is a working diagnosis, not a confirmed one.

**Plan:** education, thoracic mobilization if stiff, manual distraction (since it relieved symptoms), chin tuck and scapular setting, neural sliders if tolerated, monitor strength at each visit. Refer if wrist extension weakens or myelopathy signs appear.
**Questions and answers**

items: Why is a negative Bakody sign not enough to exclude radiculopathy? Because the sign has low sensitivity in published studies [Ref – to verify], so many true cases are negative. Always judge it with the rest of the findings.
Why check gait and Hoffmann sign in a patient with arm pain? Radiculopathy and myelopathy can coexist or be confused. Cord signs change urgency and what techniques are safe.
Why use the distraction test before choosing traction? A positive response gives a practical reason to try distraction, while a negative response gives no reason to expect benefit.
The patient says neck pain only appears on Spurling, no arm symptoms. Is it positive? No under the criterion used here. Neck pain alone shows local sensitivity, not nerve root irritation.
Wrist extension was 4/5 and is now 3/5 one week later. What do you do? This is a progressive motor deficit. Stop provocative testing, document, and arrange urgent medical review.
**Initial approach:** education and active exercise, for stable mild to moderate cases.
**Justifying findings:** root-pattern signs, no red flags, mild stable deficit.
**Priority:** education, then movement and strengthening.
**Manual therapy:** distraction (if the test was positive) and thoracic mobilization.
**Exercise:** chin tuck, scapular setting, sliders, graded strengthening.
**Modalities:** optional only, as pain relief.
**Tell the patient:** the likely course is favourable, movement is safe, report new weakness.
**Avoid:** manipulation without thorough screening, prolonged collar use, aggravating end-range compression.
**Measure:** pain scale, NDI, strength and reflexes, function.
**If no improvement:** review diagnosis, change plan, seek medical opinion.
**Referral:** cord signs, progressive deficit, red flags.
**Discharge:** minimal arm symptoms, normal function, strength restored or stable, patient confident in self-management.

blocks.text: **Assumptions:** adult, no red flags, mild stable deficit. A patient with severe or progressive weakness needs a different, medical-first plan.

Evidence strength for individual recommendations in this chapter has not yet been graded because the references have not been verified. Each **[Ref – to** **verify]** marks a claim that must receive a checked source before publication.

items: **What studies can test:** whether a test cluster raises the likelihood of radiculopathy; whether exercise plus education improves pain and function.
**Clinical implications that remain hypotheses:** that distraction or neural sliders work by reducing nerve mechanosensitivity.
**Questions for future trials:** which patients benefit most from traction; best exercise dosage; optimal reassessment timing.

sections.A: Gardan se ek nerve root nikalti hai jo baazu tak jaati hai. Jab yeh root dab jaye ya irritate ho jaye (aksar disc ya hadi ke barhne se), to dard, jhunjhunahat ya kamzori baazu mein usi nerve ke raaste par mehsoos hoti hai. Sab se zyada C6 aur C7 roots mutasir hoti hain.
sections.B: Aam taur par baazu ka dard gardan se zyada tang karta hai. Gardan peeche ya dard wali taraf ghumane se barhta hai, aur haath sar par rakhne se kam ho sakta hai. Table batata hai ke kaun si root kis ungli, kis muscle aur kis reflex se judi hai, lekin yeh sirf ishara hai, pakka saboot nahi.
sections.C: Sawal is tarah poochein ke pata chale dard kahan tak jaata hai, kamzori ya sunn-pan hai ya nahi, aur koi khatre ki nishani to nahi. Seene mein dard ke saath left arm ka dard ho to pehle dil ki wajah rule out karein.
sections.D: Examination isi tarteeb se karein: pehle dekhein, phir gardan ki movement, phir nerves ka poora check (sensation, taaqat, reflexes, dono taraf compare karein). Agar history mein shak ho to spinal cord (UMN) ka screen bhi zaroor karein.
sections.E: Yeh tests tab karein jab history radiculopathy ki taraf ishara kare aur koi red flag na ho. Spurling mein baazu ke symptoms wapas aayein to positive hai, sirf gardan ka dard positive nahi ginte. Distraction se symptoms kam hon to traction se faida ho sakta hai. Akela koi test faisla nahi karta, cluster dekhein.
sections.F: Kuch conditions bilkul isi jaisi lagti hain: myelopathy (haath bhaari, chalne mein masla), carpal ya cubital tunnel, shoulder ka dard, thoracic outlet, aur dil ki takleef. Har ek ka farq aur agla qadam table mein hai.
sections.G: Yeh khatre ki nishaniyan hain. Dono baazu ya taangon mein symptoms, tezi se barhti kamzori, peshab ya pakhane mein tabdeeli, seene ka dard, ya achanak shadeed sar dard ke saath chakkar: treatment rokein aur foran refer karein, emergency ho to emergency services bulayein.
sections.H: Faisla chaar qadmon mein: (1) emergency red flag hai? (2) myelopathy ke signs hain? (3) baazu ka dard nerve root ke pattern ke saath aur tests positive? to working diagnosis radiculopathy. (4) kamzori halki aur stable hai to conservative treatment, barh rahi hai to foran refer.
sections.I: Halke, stable case mein shuruaat education aur exercise se karein. Manual distraction sirf tab jab distraction test se symptoms kam hue hon. Thoracic mobilisation aur neural sliders bhi option hain. Yeh dawa na karein ke manual therapy disc ko theek kar deti hai. 2 se 3 sessions mein farq na pade to approach badlein.
sections.J: Exercises: chin tuck (gardan ki gehri muscles), scapular setting, neural slider, dard ke baghair movement, aur aahista taaqat barhana. Gardan ka halka dard jo jaldi theek ho jaye theek hai. Lekin agar dard baazu mein neeche tak phaile ya nayi sunn-pan ya kamzori aaye to ruk kar dobara check karein.
sections.K: Machines sirf madadgar hain, asal ilaaj nahi. Traction un patients mein soch sakte hain jin ka distraction test positive tha. TENS aur garam sikai sirf aaraam ke liye. Ultrasound, laser aur lamba collar aam taur par recommend nahi.
sections.L: Pehli visit par screen, examine aur patient ko samjhayein ke aksar log hafton ya mahinon mein behtar ho jaate hain. Phir dard kam karna, phir taaqat, phir kaam aur khel ki taraf wapsi. Koi fixed hafte nahi hote.
sections.M: Har visit par dard, NDI, gardan ki rotation, taaqat, sensation aur reflexes check karein. Behtari ho to exercise barhayein. 4 se 6 hafte mein farq na pade to diagnosis aur plan dobara dekhein. Kamzori barhe ya cord ke signs aayein to foran refer karein.
sections.N: Is case mein 42 saal ke teacher ko right C6 radiculopathy hai: angoothe ki taraf dard, wrist extension kamzor, reflex kam, aur Spurling aur distraction positive. Neeche diye sawaal khud hal karein, phir jawab dekhein.
sections.chapter-summary-treatment-decision: Mukhtasar mein: stable case mein education aur active exercise se shuru karein, red flags par nazar rakhein, har visit par taaqat aur reflexes napein, aur kamzori barhe to refer karein.
